title: Dengue killed 64 people in 13 days as experts warn of a hard December
excerpt: Nearly 24,000 people were admitted in the first 13 days of November. Doctors report more severe complications this year.

image.alt: The front of Dhaka Medical College, next to the hospital that treats many dengue patients
image.credit: Jashem farhan / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

content:
At least 64 people died of dengue and 23,880 were admitted to hospital in Bangladesh in the first 13 days of November, The Daily Star reported on 14 November, using figures from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). Experts warned that cases may not fall as fast as usual as winter approaches.

The year so far, by month

  • June: 13 deaths, 2,907 admissions.
  • July: 36 deaths, 9,206 admissions.
  • August: 43 deaths, 20,536 admissions.
  • September: 148 deaths, 43,774 admissions.
  • October: 174 deaths, about 53,000 admissions.
  • 1 to 13 November: at least 64 deaths, 23,880 admissions.

DGHS had recorded 483 deaths this year by 13 November.

What experts said

Prof Kabirul Bashar, an entomologist at Jahangirnagar University, said recent rain means the fall in cases this month may be smaller than expected, and that December could see more cases than in past years, the newspaper reported. He called for clearing breeding sites, using larvicide where water cannot be drained, and stronger action against Culex mosquitoes.

Dr HM Nazmul Ahsan, associate professor at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, said hospitals are still receiving many critically ill patients, with more liver, kidney, lung and heart complications this year. He said this may be linked to dengue virus serotype 3 (DENV-3), but more study is needed. "Early hospitalisation is our main recommendation, particularly for high-risk patients," he said.

Why it matters

Dengue is running alongside a measles outbreak that has killed more than 1,300 children, stretching the same hospitals and health workers. NGOs running community health, WASH and urban programmes can help with clean-up of breeding sites and with getting high-risk patients to hospital early.

What to watch

Whether daily admissions fall below 1,000 by the end of November, and any DGHS study on the DENV-3 serotype.

Sources

  • No respite from dengue as winter approaches, The Daily Star, 14 November 2026
